author: ribeye
dek: The CDC confirmed a third U.S. measles death of 2026 — and one Seneca County kitchen table is now buried under a decade of pediatric paperwork.
disclaimer: Parody: the Bower family of Tiffin is fictional. The measles outbreak and third U.S. death of 2026 are real, as reported by Reuters in October 2026.
headline: Tiffin Mom Digs Up Shot Records From 2011 After Nation's Worst Measles Outbreak in Decades Claims a Third Life

ohio_story: TIFFIN, Ohio — The Bower family's Tuesday started with a robocall from Tiffin City Schools and ended with Karen Bower on her knees in the hall closet, elbow-deep in a shoebox labeled "KIDS — IMPORTANT??" in fading Sharpie. Inside: a decade of report cards, a Tiffin Columbian Tornadoes ticket stub from 2019, and — finally, under a coupon for a free frosty that expired during the Obama administration — the yellow shot records for all three kids.

"I know they're vaccinated. I was there. I held the Band-Aid," Karen said, waving the crinkled cards like she'd just won the Seneca County Fair pie contest. "But the school wants proof, the pediatrician's office wants me to use the portal, and the portal wants a password I set in 2014. I have now reset my password four times, and I am no closer to proving my son had a shot in 2016 than I am to understanding the infield fly rule." Her husband, Mark, who spent the evening Googling whether measles was "the spots one or the cough one," has been reassigned to snack duty and moral support.

The kids, for their part, are treating the whole thing like a snow day that never quite arrived. Twelve-year-old Sophie has already announced she will be "working from home" if anyone so much as sneezes at the lunch table, and her little brother has asked three times whether the vaccine comes with a sticker. It does not, Karen reports, but the nurse at the Seneca County Health Department promised him a lollipop, which he has accepted as a binding legal agreement.
real_summary: The United States has logged a third measles-related death this year, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, as the country battles its worst measles outbreak in decades. The agency reported 4,410 confirmed cases nationwide as of Oct. 15, a case count not seen since the early 1990s.

The CDC had reported two measles-related deaths in September. The Department of Health and Human Services told Reuters that the National Center for Health Statistics received a report of a measles-related death and verified that the disease was the underlying cause on the death certificate. The CDC did not name the states where the deaths occurred.

Pennsylvania has been hit hardest by the resurgence, with 1,286 cases as of Oct. 19. In neighboring New York, the state health department reported 162 cases as of Oct. 17, and Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency earlier in the month. Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, but it is highly contagious and preventable through the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, which is about 97% effective after two doses.
